summary: The purpose of our project is to conduct research on the impact of the space environment on the human body through observation of the DNA of astronauts at various stages of a space mission – before, during, and after. By analyzing the differences in the genetic code of astronauts at certain periods, we seek to determine the influence of different factors of the space environment on the human organism, such as radiation, microgravity, extremely low and high temperatures, and other features of the space environment. The influence of radiation, for example, may be detrimental to DNA. Our system helps us understand how the space environment affects human biology and find out possible risks before they result in any harm to astronauts. On the basis of collected data, the project offers personalized tasks to astronauts to preserve their physical and genetic well-being.
details: This project aims to help astronauts by keeping track of any changes to their DNA and health. This uses an interlinked network of algorithms to combine various biological factors to understand how the space environment will affect the body. The main difference between this and other health tracking systems is that it takes into account the environmental factors. Using data from before, during and after space missions, this project aims to discover any possible health risks or changes to genetic information caused by factors such as exposure to radiation and microgravity. One of the main advantages of this project is that it can help astronauts keep themselves healthy. Unlike other systems that can only detect health issues, this system aims to give the astronaut specific tasks to do based on their current condition. This will help minimise the negative effects of being exposed to space. We want to help make long term space missions safer and reduce any long term health issues. We hope that we can help further space exploration by increasing our knowledge on how the human body reacts to environments outside of earth. We will be using Python, C++ and RStudio to develop our project. We shall use Python to help process data, create algorithms and analyse the relationships between factors. C++ will possibly be used to ensure our system runs efficiently. We shall use RStudio to help with any statistical analysis. We also plan to create web based algorithms to link environmental factors with health data. The creativity of our project is that we are combining environmental factors with health tracking. Most health tracking systems just look at the individuals physical wellbeing. Our project looks at how external environmental factors affect biological changes. This gives us a wider outlook on how to keep astronauts healthy. Throughout the development of our project, we took into consideration a variety of factors such as changes to DNA, radiation, heart rates, pulse, microgravity, physical activity, environmental factors and other biological reactions. We will combine these factors to create a system that will give a better understanding of astronauts health and give bespoke solutions to help keep them safe.
